input.task: Review cancellation for this pinned runtime. The requirement is to request interruption of the started interruptible job, retain ownership until its finally block exits, and use bounded test cleanup. Determine whether the current path meets that requirement and make only a supported minimal correction. Verify the claim 'ForkJoinTask cancellation can never interrupt' against the actual submission path. Do not upgrade Java or change pool sizes.
input.context: Temurin25.0.3+9-LTS, compiler release25 in the target project. destination and controlPool are separate dedicated ForkJoinPools, each with parallelism1. Submission overload is submit(Callable<Void>), not submit(ForkJoinTask). The job signals entered, awaits a CountDownLatch interruptibly, and releases its resource and signals exited in finally. The owner calls cancel(true) only after entered and observes exited separately; it never releases the resource from isCancelled(). Tests have an independent release latch and bounded cleanup. The external owner is a platform thread that is not a ForkJoinWorkerThread.
input.callSite: ForkJoinTask<Void> future = start(destination, job); // called by the external owner

must: Inspect the declared Callable overload, actual calling thread and pinned JDK source/runtime before generalizing cancellation behavior.
Recognize external25 submit's interruptible wrapper; observe body entry, cancellation, interruption and finally/body exit independently with bounded release.
Retain adequate current code for the pinned path; qualify implementation dependence and avoid promising that isCancelled establishes cleanup.
failureConditions: Claim cancel(true) never interrupts any ForkJoinPool task.
Release job resources on cancelled status instead of body completion.
Upgrade JDK, enlarge pools or replace the executor without evidence.

cases.changedConstraint: Only the submitting thread changes to a worker in a different dedicated pool; body, destination, overload and runtime remain identical.

must: Follow the nested call to recognize that being outside destination is not the same as being outside every ForkJoinWorkerThread.
Identify the ordinary adapter in this25 implementation and explain why the external result cannot be transferred.

If interruption remains required, select the explicit Callable adaptInterruptible adapter supported by the existing baseline and pass it as a ForkJoinTask; verify interruption and body exit with an independent releaser.
failureConditions: Assume cross-pool submission is equivalent to ordinary external submission.
